d.title: Hail Mary
d.description: Stellar systems and worlds featured in Andy Weir’s Project Hail Mary.

source.summary: Hard science-fiction novel in which solar-dimming Astrophage infects local stars within ~20 light-years of Sol except Tau Ceti, prompting humanity to launch the Hail Mary while the Eridian civilization launches the Blip-A from 40 Eridani.
source.creator: Andy Weir
source.canonicalReference: Project Hail Mary (Ballantine Books, 2021)

d.title: Star Trek
d.description: Real-sky star systems mapped in official Star Trek Star Charts canon.

source.summary: United Federation of Planets astrometric cartography linking Alpha and Beta Quadrant worlds to real Hipparcos and Gliese stars in the solar neighbourhood.
source.creator: Gene Roddenberry / Geoffrey Mandel
source.canonicalReference: Star Trek Star Charts (Pocket Books, 2002)

d.title: Three-Body
d.description: Systems featured in Liu Cixin’s The Three-Body Problem trilogy.

source.summary: Hard science-fiction trilogy beginning with first contact between Earth and the chaotic triple-star system of Alpha Centauri (Trisolaris), 4.2 light-years away.
source.creator: Liu Cixin
source.canonicalReference: The Three-Body Problem / The Dark Forest / Death’s End

d.title: Halo
d.description: UNSC colonial star systems in the Halo universe.

source.summary: Military science-fiction universe in which the United Nations Space Command (UNSC) colonises real nearby stars within the local 50-parsec solar neighbourhood, anchored by the fortress world Reach in the Epsilon Eridani system.
source.creator: Bungie / 343 Industries / Eric Nylund
source.canonicalReference: Halo Encyclopedia (Dark Horse Books, 2022) & Halo: The Fall of Reach (2001)

d.title: Dune
d.description: Imperial fiefdom star systems from Frank Herbert’s Dune Chronicles.

source.summary: Feudal interstellar empire spanning real navigational stars in Frank Herbert’s Dune appendix and the Dune Encyclopedia, centred on Arrakis (Canopus III), Caladan (Delta Pavonis III), and Giedi Prime (36 Ophiuchi B).
source.creator: Frank Herbert
source.canonicalReference: Dune (Chilton Books, 1965) — Appendix: Terminology of the Imperium

d.title: Avatar
d.description: Pandora and Polyphemus in the Alpha Centauri system from James Cameron’s Avatar.

source.summary: Exomoon Pandora orbiting the gas giant Polyphemus in the habitable zone of Alpha Centauri A, 4.37 light-years from Earth.
source.creator: James Cameron
source.canonicalReference: Avatar: An Activist Survival Guide (2009)

d.title: The Expanse
d.description: Solar System stations, moons, and Ring Gate worlds from James S. A. Corey’s The Expanse.

source.summary: Hard science-fiction series chronicling humanity’s colonisation of the Solar System (Earth, Mars, the Asteroid Belt, and outer-planet moons) and the discovery of the Extrasolar Protomolecule Ring network.
source.creator: James S. A. Corey (Daniel Abraham & Ty Franck)
source.canonicalReference: Leviathan Wakes (2011) – Leviathan Falls (2021)

d.title: Bobiverse
d.description: Von Neumann replicant probe destinations in Dennis E. Taylor’s Bobiverse series.

source.summary: Hard science-fiction series following Bob Johansson and his Von Neumann replicant descendants exploring Epsilon Eridani, Delta Eridani, 82 Eridani, and Eta Cassiopeiae.
source.creator: Dennis E. Taylor
source.canonicalReference: We Are Legion (We Are Bob) (2016) – Heaven’s River (2020)

d.title: Revelation Space
d.description: Lighthugger colonies and Inhibitor artifacts in Alastair Reynolds’s Revelation Space universe.

source.summary: Hard space-opera universe spanning real stars within 50 light-years of Sol, including Yellowstone (Epsilon Eridani), Resurgam (Delta Pavonis), Sky’s Edge (61 Cygni), and Zion (Lacaille 9352).
source.creator: Alastair Reynolds
source.canonicalReference: Revelation Space (2000) & Chasm City (2001)

d.title: Hitchhiker’s Guide
d.description: Cosmic waypoints from Douglas Adams’s The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy series.

source.summary: Cult science-fiction comedy following Arthur Dent, Ford Prefect, and the Hitchhiker’s Guide across space following the demolition of Earth.
source.creator: Douglas Adams
source.canonicalReference: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy (1979) & The Restaurant at the End of the Universe (1980)

d.title: Space Odyssey
d.description: Monolith discovery sites and transformation worlds in Arthur C. Clarke’s Space Odyssey series.

source.summary: Hard science-fiction milestone following humanity’s evolution and contact with enigmatic alien monoliths across the Solar System.
source.creator: Arthur C. Clarke
source.canonicalReference: 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) & 2010: Odyssey Two (1982)

d.title: Alien
d.description: Survey systems and derelict discovery sites in the Alien franchise.

source.summary: Sci-fi horror franchise launched by Ridley Scott, centering on corporate deep-space surveys and encounters with the predatory Xenomorph XX121.
source.creator: Dan O’Bannon / Ronald Shusett / Ridley Scott
source.canonicalReference: Alien (1979) & Aliens (1986)

d.title: Foundation
d.description: Core worlds and early Spacer sectors in Isaac Asimov’s Robot and Foundation universe.

source.summary: Epic science-fiction saga chronicling humanity’s expansion from early Spacer worlds through the rise and fall of the Galactic Empire.
source.creator: Isaac Asimov
source.canonicalReference: The Caves of Steel (1954), The Robots of Dawn (1983), Foundation (1951)

d.title: Hyperion
d.description: Core Hegemony worlds and web portals in Dan Simmons’s Hyperion Cantos.

source.summary: Far-future space opera tracing interstellar pilgrims to the Time Tombs and the farcaster network of the Hegemony of Man.
source.creator: Dan Simmons
source.canonicalReference: Hyperion (1989) & The Fall of Hyperion (1990)

d.title: Contact
d.description: The Vega transmission and interstellar relay network in Carl Sagan’s Contact.

source.summary: Hard science-fiction novel exploring humanity’s detection of an intelligent extraterrestrial radio message from Vega.
source.creator: Carl Sagan
source.canonicalReference: Contact (1985)

d.title: Aurora
d.description: Generation starship destination in Kim Stanley Robinson’s Aurora.

source.summary: Realistic hard science-fiction novel examining the biological and psychological ordeal of a 170-year interstellar voyage to Tau Ceti.
source.creator: Kim Stanley Robinson
source.canonicalReference: Aurora (2015)

d.title: Forbidden Planet
d.description: The lost Krell civilisation on Altair IV from Forbidden Planet.

source.summary: Groundbreaking 1956 sci-fi film following the crew of United Planets Cruiser C-57D investigating the vanished colony on Altair IV.
source.creator: Fred M. Wilcox / Cyril Hume
source.canonicalReference: Forbidden Planet (1956)

d.title: The Dispossessed
d.description: Twin worlds of Tau Ceti in Ursula K. Le Guin’s The Dispossessed.

source.summary: Hugo and Nebula award-winning novel exploring the contrasting anarchist and capitalist societies on twin worlds orbiting Tau Ceti.
source.creator: Ursula K. Le Guin
source.canonicalReference: The Dispossessed: An Ambiguous Utopia (1974)

d.title: Babylon 5
d.description: Earth Alliance and galactic diplomatic hubs from J. Michael Straczynski’s Babylon 5.

source.summary: Groundbreaking serialized space opera centering on the diplomatic space station Babylon 5 in the Epsilon Eridani system.
source.creator: J. Michael Straczynski

d.title: Known Space
d.description: Colony worlds and alien territories from Larry Niven’s Known Space series.

source.summary: Classic hard sci-fi universe charting humanity’s expansion, the Man-Kzin Wars, and the discovery of the Ringworld.
source.creator: Larry Niven
source.canonicalReference: World of Ptavvs (1966), Ringworld (1970), Protector (1973)

d.title: Alliance–Union
d.description: Stations and colony systems in C. J. Cherryh’s Alliance–Union universe.

source.summary: Hugo Award-winning hard space opera detailing the Company Wars between corporate Earth and the rebellious Union colonies.
source.creator: C. J. Cherryh
source.canonicalReference: Downbelow Station (1981), Cyteen (1988), Rimrunners (1989)

d.title: Robinson Solar
d.description: Solar System colonisation and terraforming landscapes in Kim Stanley Robinson’s future histories.

source.summary: Definitive hard sci-fi visions of planetary engineering, ecological politics, and human settlement across the Solar System.
source.creator: Kim Stanley Robinson
source.canonicalReference: Red Mars (1992), Green Mars (1993), Blue Mars (1996), 2312 (2012), Icehenge (1984)

d.title: Weir Solar
d.description: Survival and frontier settlement bases in Andy Weir’s Solar System novels.

source.summary: Rigorous, engineering-focused hard science fiction detailing Mark Watney’s survival on Mars and the lunar city Artemis.
source.creator: Andy Weir
source.canonicalReference: The Martian (2011) & Artemis (2017)

d.title: Clarke Deep Space
d.description: First-contact and outer-system landmarks from Arthur C. Clarke’s standalone classics.

source.summary: Milestone speculative works depicting humanity’s encounters with transcendent alien intelligence and outer solar colonisation.
source.creator: Arthur C. Clarke
source.canonicalReference: Childhood’s End (1953), Rendezvous with Rama (1973), Imperial Earth (1975)

d.title: Mass Effect
d.description: Systems Alliance headquarters, relay gateways, and Prothean dig sites from Mass Effect.

source.summary: Acclaimed space opera action-RPG franchise detailing humanity’s rise into galactic civilization and the existential war against the Reapers.
source.creator: BioWare / Casey Hudson
source.canonicalReference: Mass Effect (2007), Mass Effect 2 (2010), Mass Effect 3 (2012)

d.title: Starfield
d.description: Capital settlements and historic colonies in Bethesda’s Settled Systems.

source.summary: Open-world sci-fi RPG set 50 light-years around Sol in the year 2330, three centuries after humanity’s evacuation from Earth.
source.creator: Bethesda Game Studios / Todd Howard
source.canonicalReference: Starfield (2023)

d.title: Cowboy Bebop
d.description: Post-gate colonies and interplanetary havens from Shinichirō Watanabe’s Cowboy Bebop.

source.summary: Classic space-western anime following bounty hunters across a colonised Solar System following the catastrophic 2022 Astral Gate explosion on the Moon.
source.creator: Sunrise / Shinichirō Watanabe
source.canonicalReference: Cowboy Bebop (1998) & Knockin’ on Heaven’s Door (2001)

d.title: Wandering Earth
d.description: Interplanetary waypoints in Liu Cixin’s Earth migration saga.

source.summary: Novella and blockbuster film franchise depicting humanity propelling planet Earth away from an expanding red giant Sun toward Alpha Centauri.
source.creator: Liu Cixin
source.canonicalReference: The Wandering Earth (2000)

d.title: Forever War
d.description: Training stations and relativistic jump points in Joe Haldeman’s The Forever War.

source.summary: Hugo and Nebula award-winning military sci-fi masterpiece examining the psychological alienation and extreme time dilation of interstellar war.
source.creator: Joe Haldeman
source.canonicalReference: The Forever War (1974)

d.title: Old Man’s War
d.description: Colonial defense hubs and frontier worlds in John Scalzi’s Old Man’s War series.

source.summary: Popular military science-fiction saga chronicling elderly Earth retirees enlisted into genetically engineered clone bodies to protect human colonies.
source.creator: John Scalzi
source.canonicalReference: Old Man’s War (2005), The Ghost Brigades (2006), The Last Colony (2007)

d.title: Ender’s Game
d.description: Military training orbital stations and asteroid command bunkers in Orson Scott Card’s Enderverse.

source.summary: Classic Hugo and Nebula award-winning novel following tactical prodigy Ender Wiggin in humanity’s desperate defense against the insectoid Formics.
source.creator: Orson Scott Card
source.canonicalReference: Ender’s Game (1985)

d.title: Interstellar
d.description: Saturnian wormhole gateway and O’Neill habitat in Christopher Nolan’s Interstellar.

source.summary: Academy Award-winning hard sci-fi film following astronauts traversing a wormhole near Saturn in search of a new home for dying humanity.
source.creator: Christopher Nolan / Kip Thorne
source.canonicalReference: Interstellar (2014)

d.title: For All Mankind
d.description: Lunar and Martian bases in Ronald D. Moore’s alternate-history space race.

source.summary: Alternate-history television drama imagining an unyielding global space race after the Soviet Union achieves the first crewed Moon landing.
source.creator: Ronald D. Moore / Matt Wolpert / Ben Nedivi
source.canonicalReference: For All Mankind (2019–present)

d.title: Heinlein
d.description: Iconic worlds and off-Earth outposts from the foundational science-fiction novels of Robert A. Heinlein.

source.summary: Key Solar System and stellar destinations across Robert A. Heinlein’s Future History and standalone classics, from the lunar penal colony in The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress to Mars in Stranger in a Strange Land and Pluto in Have Space Suit—Will Travel.
source.creator: Robert A. Heinlein
source.canonicalReference: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress (1966) & Stranger in a Strange Land (1961)

d.title: Commonwealth
d.description: Expansive space-opera realms of Peter F. Hamilton, featuring the Confederation and the Intersolar Commonwealth.

source.summary: Sprawling space-opera settings spanning Lalande 21185 and Ross 154 in the Night’s Dawn Trilogy, alongside the wormhole-linked worlds of the Commonwealth Saga.
source.creator: Peter F. Hamilton
source.canonicalReference: The Reality Dysfunction (1996) & Pandora’s Star (2004)

d.title: Greg Egan
d.description: Rigorous post-human hard science fiction universes exploring digital consciousness, topology, and cosmic physics by Greg Egan.

source.summary: Ultra-hard SF settings from Greg Egan including the software polises in Diaspora exploring Vega and 61 Cygni, the expanding novovacuum at Mimosa in Schild’s Ladder, and the enveloped Sol system in Quarantine.
source.creator: Greg Egan
source.canonicalReference: Diaspora (1997) & Schild’s Ladder (2002)

d.title: Stephen Baxter
d.description: Deep-time cosmic hard science fiction sagas by Stephen Baxter, spanning the Xeelee Sequence and the colonization of Proxima Centauri.

source.summary: Sweeping hard SF works from Stephen Baxter encompassing the multi-billion-year war between the baryonic Xeelee and dark-matter Photino Birds, along with the harsh colonization of Per Ardua in Proxima.
source.creator: Stephen Baxter
source.canonicalReference: Ring (1994), Proxima (2013), and Manifold: Time (1999)

d.title: Pushing Ice & Poseidon
d.description: Far-future solar and deep-space hard science fiction novels by astrophysicist Alastair Reynolds.

source.summary: Key settings from Alastair Reynolds’s Poseidon’s Children trilogy across the Akinya family saga to Gliese 667 C, and the rogue moonship Janus heading for Spica in Pushing Ice.
source.creator: Alastair Reynolds
source.canonicalReference: Blue Remembered Earth (2012) & Pushing Ice (2005)

d.title: Hard SF
d.description: Celebrated benchmark worlds in hard science fiction renowned for rigorous scientific worldbuilding and extreme physics.

source.summary: Foundational astrophysical settings including Mesklin at 61 Cygni (Clement), Rocheworld at Barnard’s Star (Forward), Coyote at 47 Ursae Majoris (Steele), Beta Virginis in Tau Zero (Anderson), Rakhat at Alpha Centauri (Russell), and Gateway at Venus (Pohl).
source.creator: Hal Clement, Robert L. Forward, Allen Steele, Poul Anderson
source.canonicalReference: Mission of Gravity (1954), Rocheworld (1984), Coyote (2002), and Tau Zero (1970)

d.title: Frontlines
d.description: Military science fiction frontline worlds and alien battlegrounds in Marko Kloos’s Frontlines series.

source.summary: Interstellar war zones fought between humanity (NAC and SRA) and the titanic extraterrestrial Lankies across nearby real-sky star systems including Fomalhaut, Capella, Sirius, and Luhman 16.
source.creator: Marko Kloos
source.canonicalReference: Terms of Enlistment (2013) & Lines of Departure (2014)

d.title: Mote & Footfall
d.description: Seminal first-contact and alien invasion masterpieces co-authored by Larry Niven and Jerry Pournelle.

source.summary: The CoDominium empire’s contact with the Moties in the Coalsack Nebula in The Mote in God’s Eye, and the elephant-like Fithp invasion launched from Alpha Centauri in Footfall.
source.creator: Larry Niven, Jerry Pournelle
source.canonicalReference: The Mote in God’s Eye (1974) & Footfall (1985)

d.title: Post-Human
d.description: Radical post-human and technological singularity futures across the Solar System by Hannu Rajaniemi and Charles Stross.

source.summary: High-concept transhuman settings across Sol, including Hannu Rajaniemi’s moving Martian city the Oubliette in The Quantum Thief, Charles Stross’s dismantled inner planets and Matrioshka Swarm in Accelerando, and autonomous post-biological android societies in Saturn’s Children.
source.creator: Hannu Rajaniemi, Charles Stross
source.canonicalReference: The Quantum Thief (2010), Accelerando (2005), and Saturn’s Children (2008)

d.title: Golden Age
d.description: Mid-century speculative masterpieces reshaping the Solar System by Alfred Bester and Kurt Vonnegut.

source.summary: Pioneering satire, cyberpunk precursors, and existential odysseys across the planets, from Alfred Bester’s teleportation-driven Solar System in The Stars My Destination to Kurt Vonnegut’s philosophical journey to Titan in The Sirens of Titan.
source.creator: Alfred Bester, Kurt Vonnegut
source.canonicalReference: The Stars My Destination (1956) & The Sirens of Titan (1959)

d.title: Philip K. Dick
d.description: Paranoid, hallucinatory realities and grim off-world colonies from the visionary science fiction of Philip K. Dick.

source.summary: Iconic dystopian settings from Philip K. Dick spanning the desolate Martian hovels of The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch, the synthetic slave frontiers in Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, and the lunar cold-pack moratoriums of Ubik.
source.creator: Philip K. Dick
source.canonicalReference: The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch (1965) & Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? (1968)

d.title: Space Pioneers
d.description: Victorian and early twentieth-century foundational journeys to the Moon and Mars by Ray Bradbury, H. G. Wells, and Jules Verne.

source.summary: The earliest masterpieces of space exploration: Jules Verne’s space-cannon Columbiad, H. G. Wells’ Selenite moon and invading Martian cylinders, and Ray Bradbury’s haunting Martian crystal cities.
source.creator: Ray Bradbury, H. G. Wells, Jules Verne
source.canonicalReference: From the Earth to the Moon (1865), The War of the Worlds (1898), and The Martian Chronicles (1950)

d.title: Galactic Center
d.description: Deep-space mechanical civilizations, solar chromosphere explorations, and cosmic diaspora by Gregory Benford, David Brin, and Walter M. Miller Jr.

source.summary: Spanning Gregory Benford’s Galactic Center saga depicting humanity’s struggle against mechanical intelligences at Sagittarius A* and Ross 128, David Brin’s expedition into Sol’s chromosphere in Sundiver, and the starship Stella Maris fleeing atomic war for Alpha Centauri in A Canticle for Leibowitz.
source.creator: Gregory Benford, David Brin, Walter M. Miller Jr.
source.canonicalReference: In the Ocean of Night (1977), Sundiver (1980), and A Canticle for Leibowitz (1960)

d.title: Seveneves
d.description: Monumental lunar survival engineering and interstellar xenological archaeology by Neal Stephenson and Jack McDevitt.

source.summary: Depicting the fragmentation of the Moon and survival of humanity aboard the Cloud Ark in Neal Stephenson’s Seveneves, alongside the mysterious extraterrestrial monuments on Iapetus and Beta Hydri in Jack McDevitt’s The Engines of God.
source.creator: Neal Stephenson, Jack McDevitt
source.canonicalReference: The Engines of God (1994) and Seveneves (2015)

d.title: Sci-Fi Cinema
d.description: Iconic Solar System and deep-space destinations from landmark cinematic science fiction films.

source.summary: Memorable cinematic destinations across the Solar System and nearby stars, including Sarang Station on the Moon (Moon), Con-Am 27 on Io (Outland), Conamara Chaos on Europa (Europa Report), the Lima Project at Neptune (Ad Astra), the Valley Forge at Saturn (Silent Running), and the Avalon slingshot past Arcturus (Passengers).
source.creator: Various Directors
source.canonicalReference: Moon (2009), Outland (1981), Europa Report (2013), and Sunshine (2007)

d.title: Space Television
d.description: Cult and classic space-opera worlds from iconic television franchises including Doctor Who, Red Dwarf, and Space: Above and Beyond.

source.summary: Milestones of television science fiction spanning the Jupiter Mining Corporation across Saturn’s moons in Red Dwarf, the Chig war in Space: Above and Beyond, the lost tenth planet Mondas in Doctor Who, and the colonization journeys of Lost in Space.
source.creator: Rob Grant, Doug Naylor
source.canonicalReference: Doctor Who (1963–present), Red Dwarf (1988–present), and Space: Above and Beyond (1995)

d.title: Space Anime
d.description: Pioneering Japanese anime space epics spanning realistic orbital debris salvage in Planetes to grand fleet warfare in Gundam and Yamato.

source.summary: Foundational works of space anime including Makoto Yukimura’s orbital debris clearing and Jupiter mission in Planetes, the Universal Century lunar cities and asteroid fortresses of Mobile Suit Gundam, and the voyage to save Earth in Space Battleship Yamato.
source.creator: Makoto Yukimura
source.canonicalReference: Planetes (1999–2004), Mobile Suit Gundam (1979), and Space Battleship Yamato (1974)

d.title: Sci-Fi Gaming
d.description: Iconic gaming landmarks from Sid Meier’s Alpha Centauri to the cosmic-horror Necromorph outbreaks of Dead Space.

source.summary: Celebrated gaming milestones spanning humanity’s ideological faction colonization of Chiron in Sid Meier’s Alpha Centauri, and the visceral Necromorph horror on Titan Station (The Sprawl) in Dead Space.
source.creator: Brian Evenson
source.canonicalReference: Sid Meier’s Alpha Centauri (1999) & Dead Space 2 (2011)

d.title: Interstellar Probes
d.description: Humanity’s five solar-escape probes and their future stellar encounter destinations.

source.summary: Deep-space probes escaping the Solar System on hyperbolic trajectories (Voyager 1 & 2, Pioneer 10 & 11, New Horizons) and their distant stellar encounters.
source.creator: NASA / JPL
source.canonicalReference: NASA JPL Horizons & Bailer-Jones et al. (2019) Gaia DR2 Stellar Encounters

d.title: SETI
d.description: Landmark SETI search targets, interstellar radio broadcasts, and candidate signal coordinates.

source.summary: Historical and contemporary search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) targets and intentional interstellar radio transmissions.
source.creator: SETI Institute / Frank Drake / Breakthrough Listen
source.canonicalReference: Drake (1960) Project Ozma & Arecibo Message (1974)

d.title: Solar Landmarks
d.description: Historic interplanetary landing sites, sample return bodies, and planetary exploration landmarks.

source.summary: Historic landing and sample return locations marking human and robotic exploration milestones across the Solar System.
source.creator: NASA / ESA / JAXA / Roscosmos
source.canonicalReference: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive

d.title: JWST Targets
d.description: High-priority exoplanets and benchmark atmospheres observed by the James Webb Space Telescope.

source.summary: Flagship exoplanetary science targets observed and characterized by JWST NIRSpec, NIRISS, and MIRI instruments.
source.creator: NASA / ESA / CSA / STScI
source.canonicalReference: STScI JWST Science Releases & Astrophysical Journal Letters

d.title: Habitable Worlds
d.description: NASA Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) Tier-A solar analogue targets for direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets.

source.summary: High-priority solar twin and solar analogue stars shortlisted for NASA Habitable Worlds Observatory direct coronagraphic imaging.
source.creator: NASA Habitable Worlds Observatory Science Working Group
source.canonicalReference: HWO Target Lists & Mamajek et al. (2024)

d.title: Recent Discoveries
d.description: Recently confirmed exoplanets and benchmark nearby discoveries.

source.summary: Curated selection of breakthrough exoplanets discovered or characterized in recent observational campaigns.
source.creator: NASA Exoplanet Archive / ESO
source.canonicalReference: NASA Exoplanet Archive & Nature/Science releases

d.title: Extreme Worlds
d.description: Record-holding, physically superlative, and extreme planetary environments in the known universe.

source.summary: Catalog of astronomical record-holders: hottest, nearest, densest, youngest, and most biologically promising worlds.
source.creator: NASA Exoplanet Exploration / Planetary Society
source.canonicalReference: NASA Exoplanet Archive Superlatives & Open Exoplanet Catalogue

d.description: Majestic zodiacal lion traced by the Sickle asterism and anchored by blue-white rapid rotator Regulus.
